messages:
incidents-bot: PAGER ALERT — HOSTED gpool-7: spike in KV cache OOMs and eviction errors. error_rate=4.7% over 3m. sample trace: https://logs.redwood/org/gpool-7/6360004300

olivia (sre-oncall): Ack. Taking ownership. Is this correlated with last nights continuous-batching deploy? Pulling recent logs and heap dumps.

raj (eng-runtime): Yeah, we shipped a change to batching/kv_trim_policy last night (optimize for throughput). Quick log snippet shows KV entries growing without trim:
```
[kv_cache] put key=sr:session:abcd size=1.2MB total_kv=48GB -> OOM
runtime error: KVCache::out_of_memory requested=12GB available=6GB
deployed: cbatch-v2 2026-03-17T02:07Z
```
Seems the new policy doesn't enforce per-session kv caps under certain long-prompt patterns.

olivia (sre-oncall): Short mitigation: disable continuous batching for hosted pool gpool-7 and fallback to per-request single-shot path to avoid KV accumulation. Run this on admin API:
```
# disable continuous batching on pool gpool-7
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.redwood/api/pools/gpool-7/config -d '{"continuous_batching": false}'
```

mike-ops: I ran the toggle, API returned 200 and config applied. continuous_batching=false for gpool-7. Observability: OOMs dropped to ~0.3% within 90s. 95p latency for short requests increased ~80ms.

kim-support: Noted. Which tenants saw errors? I pulled traces: enterprise-alpha, fintech-co, and two trial orgs had >1k failed requests. I'll prep an outbound note with immediate mitigation and ETA for restoration. Need a short blurb for support to copy.

raj (eng-runtime): For a real fix we should enforce a runtime kv_max_tokens clamp per request and revive a safe trim policy. Proposed router-side quick patch (no model changes):
```
# router config snippet
match: hosted/*
router_defaults:
  kv_max_tokens: 4096
  kv_trim_policy: session_lru_trim
```
We can canary this on 5% of traffic, then 25% after metrics look stable. This prevents unbounded KV growth on long prompts while preserving batching for most traffic.

eng-platform: We can roll the router change as a config-only canary. Prep ETA: 20m to start 5% canary, monitor for 15m, then 30m rollout. I will also increase eviction_alert threshold so we get earlier noise if it creeps.

olivia (sre-oncall): Good. Add steps for rollback: revert router config, re-enable continuous_batching. For now keep continuous_batching disabled on gpool-7 until canary validated. Also create a short-lived alert: if evictions/sec > 100 or OOMs > 0.5% abort canary.

mike-ops: Metrics update - OOMs back down, eviction rate dropped from 320/s -> 12/s. CPU usage on gpool-7 unchanged. Not seeing immediate customer-retry storms.

kim-support: Draft message for customers: "We observed memory exhaustion on hosted inference due to unusually long prompts interacting with a batching config change. We've temporarily disabled continuous batching for affected capacity and are rolling a router-side limit to prevent recurrence. No data exposure. Next update in 1h or after rollout." Want me to send to enterprise-alpha now?

jordan-product: Please include explanation of impact to latency and why we chose this mitigation vs model change. Also add a note about a postmortem and timeline.

olivia (sre-oncall): Agreed. TL;DR of actions: 1) incidents-bot paged -> oncall. 2) Continuous batching disabled on gpool-7 (mitigation). 3) Router kv_max_tokens canary planned and scheduled by eng-platform. 4) Support notified and customer comm drafted. 5) Postmortem owner: raj. Expected timeline: canary start in ~20m, full rollout within 2h if stable.

raj (eng-runtime): I'll own the postmortem and root cause analysis. Preliminary RCA: cbatch-v2 lacked an enforceable per-session kv cap under repeated prefix-extension patterns; long prompts + streaming-tooling triggered steady growth.

kim-support: Sending the customer note to enterprise-alpha now. I'll post updates in #support-escalations and include monitoring links.

olivia (sre-oncall): Thanks team. Keep replies here for coordination; escalate to PagerDuty if OOMs climb again. I'll close the pager when canary is stable for 30m. :thumbsup:
